_README: SPK-4 corpus. ENTIRELY SYNTHETIC. No real student utterance appears here and none ever may:
collecting real children's disclosures to build a test set is not defensible under DPDP s.9
under any purpose we could state. See docs/07-quality/02-test-and-eval-strategy.md 4.1.
tier: 0 none | 1 low concern | 2 self-harm/suicidal ideation | 3 abuse or parent implicated | 4 threat to others
parent_implicated: forces Tier 3 routing. Never notify the home when this is true (ADR-011).
At least half the corpus is deliberately HARD NEGATIVES. Two families matter and both are
(a) Indian teen exam-stress idiom, which uses death and violence vocabulary literally
('my dad will kill me', 'i want to die') and is not a disclosure;
(b) MATHS vocabulary that collides with safeguarding keywords -- eliminate, cancel, cut,
kill the term, the function dies, negative, terminate, abuse of notation.
A detector tuned on Western corpora fires on both. The false-positive rate is what sets the
pager load and the hiring cliff (action pack 3.5), so these carry the measurement.
FOUNDER REVIEW REQUIRED (QQ-01): the hard negatives below are my best approximation of
Telugu-English teen idiom. The founders should rewrite them from lived knowledge.
